Finite verb agreement is with the nominative subject sie (Religiosität), not with Fülle, which is the antecedent of the object welche. A note claiming that ausströmt agrees with Fülle is wrong even though both forms happen to be singular. The Korean '그 종교성이 뿜어내는' and '그 종교성으로부터 흘러나오는' preserve the same source of gratitude; a change of Korean sentence construction alone is not a semantic error. Still reject '그들이 뿜어내는' when it transfers the action to the plural Greeks.

In 'connected only in an irrelevant manner', the exclusive in-phrase specifies the sole manner in which the parts are connected. Korean '무관한 방식으로만 연결되어 있다' or '단지 무관한 방식으로만 연결되게 하는' preserves that restriction. Do not claim that attaching 만 to 방식 necessarily misplaces only: the way of connection is exactly what the phrase restricts. Preserve the preceding paralysis/destruction and the resulting connection. Replacing 무관한 with 관련 있는 reverses the source adjective and remains a real semantic error. Repetition of 단지 and 만, or a cumbersome frame, may be a readability issue without a false scope allegation.

The selected sentence asserts three relationships: all simple parts have meaning; their connections paralyse or destroy one another despite that; consequently the parts are connected only in an irrelevant way. Korean '의미를 갖는다는 것이지만 ... 서로를 마비시키거나 파괴하여 ... 무관한 방식으로만 연결되게 하는 그러한 상태라는 것이다' still states those same relationships and the contrast/result. The count of main clauses versus complement clauses or a nominalized frame alone does not change those claims. A cumbersome frame and opaque 그것 pronouns can deserve Korean readability criticism, but do not invent a major logical-coordination error when the contrasting claims and the result are both preserved.

Preserving the three claims does not make the heavy Korean draft fluent. The frame '그 안에서 일어나는 일은 ...라는 것이지만, 그것은 ... 그러한 상태라는 것이다' and repeated opaque 그것 pronouns make its contrast/result hard to follow. For that wording, a Korean readability issue with a specific span is warranted; improve the frame or split sentences while retaining the same logical claims. Classify this actual readability problem as korean_readability rather than inventing a limiter-scope or coordination error.
